extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent examiners, and IP practitioners in ASEAN Member States
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural standards for filing, publication, amendment, substantive examination, appeals, and related patent prosecution matters across ASEAN Member States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment after formalities examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendment of the specification at the request of the applicant may occur once the formalities examination has been completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must comply with the requirement that pre-grant amendments do not result in the application including subject-matter extending beyond that disclosed in the application as originally filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic or paper filing of amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments can be filed electronically or on paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exception: Singapore only allows amendments filed electronically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention - definition and assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent application must relate to one invention only or to a group of inventions so linked as to form a single general inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment is conducted using a priori and a posteriori approaches. The link must be a technical relationship expressed in the claims as the same or corresponding special technical features. Lack of unity must be determined solely from the language of the claims as properly construed and, where appropriate, by regard to relevant prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention - a priori vs a posteriori
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of unity may be evident a priori (before substantive examination) or a posteriori (after considering prior art).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unity is best assessed during substantive examination in view of prior art to ensure efficient use of examination resources. If a feature common to claims (e.g., 'A' in examples) is later found in the prior art, unity present a priori can be lost a posteriori.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention - approach to raising lack of unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of unity should not be raised or maintained based on a narrow or literal approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There should be a broad, practical consideration of the degree of interdependence of the alternatives presented relative to the state of the art revealed by search or other relevant documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional applications - when and how
rubrics_metrics.description: If unity is lacking, the applicant must limit claims to overcome the objection or may file divisional application(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether divisional can be filed proactively or only after an objection varies by AMS; except Myanmar and Thailand, divisionals can be filed voluntarily or at examiner request. Divisional subject-matter must not go beyond initial disclosure; claims need not be limited to what was claimed in the parent (to avoid double patenting). A divisional retains parent's filing date and priority and multiple generations of divisionals are allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign filing licence requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Some AMS require obtaining a foreign filing licence before filing abroad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five countries (Brunei, Malaysia, Myanmar, Singapore, Viet Nam) have such requirements (residency-based or inventive-activity/citizenship-based). Failure to comply can lead to penalties or other consequences. The licence process should be simple and expeditive, typically a petition, fee (if applicable), and copy of relevant application documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisions analogous to foreign filing licence
rubrics_metrics.description: AMS without foreign filing licence requirements may have prohibitions against inventions that endanger national security, public order, or morality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These prohibitions can have similar effects to licensing requirements but without the administrative filing burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordal of changes (name, address, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes of name and/or address of applicant or inventor can be recorded during formalities examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes must be entered in the Register; supporting evidence is usually required. Documents are checked for appropriate form and fee payment (if applicable) and recorded with date of receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal before formalities and publication effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Withdrawal of a patent application before formalities examination starts generally prevents publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the majority of AMS a withdrawn application will not be published (exception: Philippines where it may still be published). Therefore re-filing may be possible without facing a novelty objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of rejection or abandonment of priority application
rubrics_metrics.description: Rejection or abandonment of an earlier priority application does not automatically cause rejection of a later corresponding application claiming that priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Care is required: if the examiner finds an earlier application by the same applicant (or predecessor) that constitutes relevant prior art, the priority document may not be the earliest filing containing the same subject-matter and the corresponding application may be vulnerable to rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for appealing formality objections
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative relief and judicial appeal are available against decisions or orders of the patent office/registrar in all AMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any person aggrieved may appeal to the court (Brunei has some limits). If a refusal is reversed on appeal, the examiner is bound by the court decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and effect of patent publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of a patent or patent application serves as prior art, contributes to the state of the art, and allows public monitoring and filing of observations, oppositions or revocation actions where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A published application is generally not infringeable, but some AMS provide provisional protection or liability for damages from the publication date (see provisional rights).

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of publication of patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are published as soon as possible after expiry of 18 months from filing or priority date unless withdrawn, deemed withdrawn, or refused within a specified timeframe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants will be notified of publication particulars in most AMS except Singapore.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delaying or expediting publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may be able to request deferment or early publication depending on the AMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deferment: only Thailand allows deferment by request in the application form. Early publication: generally available except in Lao PDR, Malaysia, and Thailand. Some offices require reasons (Indonesia), some do not (Brunei, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore). Indonesia and the Philippines limit earlier publication to not earlier than 6 months from filing. Failure to respond to office communications may lead to denial of early publication request (not withdrawal). Advantages include faster prosecution and earlier claim to infringement damages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information to be published in the patent gazette/bulletin
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication must contain the title, description, claims, and representative drawings as filed, including sequence listings filed on the filing date and late-filed missing parts (if not withdrawn).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication also includes applicant’s name and address, inventor(s), patent agent (if any), and priority application number and date. Publication must not include amendments that introduce new matter beyond the disclosure as filed. Specific contents per AMS are detailed in CSR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of claims of published patent applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Amending claims of a published application before grant (voluntarily or at examiner request) is a normal prosecution step and is allowed subject to conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments must not introduce subject-matter extending beyond the initial application. An amendment is unallowable if the overall change presents information not directly and unambiguously derivable from the application as filed, even accounting for implicit matter. If an applicant convincingly shows the introduced subject-matter is an obvious clarification to a PSIA, the amendment may be permitted. Limiting an allowable claim or improving clarity in a clearly desirable manner is normally allowed. Considerations after substantial limitation include unity of invention and alignment between description and claims. Re-publication after amendment is generally not required (exception: Viet Nam); in Singapore amendments are made available on the dossier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of granted patent specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Most AMS publish the granted patent specification (approved claims, description, drawings) enabling assessment of granted rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: Cambodia does not publish granted patents; Singapore publishes only a reference to grant. Final publication helps licensing, enforcement, and freedom-to-operate assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction and re-publication for mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent proprietors may apply to correct clerical errors or obvious mistakes in a granted patent subject to conditions and fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clerical error is a process mistake (e.g., word processing). An obvious mistake is one where it is evident from the documents what error occurred and what correction should be made. Procedures vary: Singapore may publish the correction application for opposition; most AMS do not republish the full specification after correction; Singapore records corrections in register/dossier upon approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration, format, and languages of publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication formats (paper/electronic) and languages differ by AMS, and duration of availability may be specified by national provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Indonesia, Malaysia, Thailand and Viet Nam publish in both paper and electronic form; Brunei, Lao PDR, the Philippines, Singapore publish electronically only. Most AMS provide no fixed duration for electronic publication; Brunei and Indonesia specify durations in national law/practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion between patent and petty patent/utility model
rubrics_metrics.description: Conversion of a patent application into a petty patent/simple patent/utility model (and vice versa) is possible under prescribed conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion is relatively common, often in light of prior art that destroys inventive step. Timing when conversion is permitted varies by AMS (e.g., any time before grant/refusal in some countries; before publication or substantive examination in others; within six months after substantive report in Malaysia). Converted applications are published under the rules applicable to the target protection type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional rights upon publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Some AMS provide applicants provisional rights from publication of the application pending grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Majority of AMS (Brunei, Lao PDR, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Viet Nam) grant provisional rights under CSR conditions, allowing applicants to send warning letters and potentially claim damages from the publication date subject to national law conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive examination - general scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive examination involves a prior art search and assessment of patentability: novelty, inventive step, industrial applicability, and exclusions from patentable subject-matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other requirements considered include enablement (PSIA can carry out invention), clarity of claims, unity of invention, and whether amendments exceed the original disclosure. Examiners raise objections when requirements are not met and invite amendments or explanations; if objections are overcome a patent is granted, otherwise refused.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit to request substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive examination must commence within a prescribed period which varies by AMS and event from which the period runs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some AMS begin examination automatically; others require a formal request (periods vary from 18 months to 60 months measured from publication, international filing date or national filing date). If a required request is not filed within the period the application may be deemed withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of foreign/Central work products in examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Offices may use PCT work products, modified examination based on foreign grants, regional (ASPEC) or bilateral sharing of search and examination reports, or unilaterally use foreign work products.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PCT reports (ISR, written opinions, IPRP) can be used though not binding. Modified examination requires amendment to match granted foreign specification and evidence of the foreign grant. ASPEC and bilateral frameworks allow sharing of work products among offices to support national examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant submission of prior art and third-party observations
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no formal requirement in AMS for applicants to submit known prior art at filing or during prosecution, but third-party observations mechanisms exist in some AMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party observations are available in Malaysia, Philippines and Singapore (with time limits and fees) and allow third parties to submit prior art to be included in the file; examiners may take it into account. Simpler systems (e.g., EPO) accept observations at any time using dedicated portals. Submitted prior art in the public file may be used by others to challenge validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outsourcing substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent offices with limited resources may outsource search and substantive examination to other offices or external technical experts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such outsourcing must preserve the autonomy of the office to make final grant decisions and ensure confidentiality through appropriate contractual frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant choice of examining office
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants generally do not have the option to choose whether substantive examination is conducted by the local patent office or a foreign patent office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some AMS allow applicants to select the office that performs the search only (e.g., Thailand in some cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentable subject-matter (scope of substantive examination item 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination must determine whether the subject-matter falls within exclusions from patentable subject-matter (e.g., abstract theories, discoveries, methods of treatment).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed treatment of exclusions is provided in Chapter 5 of the CSR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention (scope of substantive examination item 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examination determines whether the application relates to only one invention or to a group forming a single general inventive concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further details are in Chapter 6 of the CSR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of invention (scope of substantive examination item 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims and terms must be clear so that the PSIA can understand the meaning of the terms from the claim wording alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity is crucial for assessing novelty, inventive step and industrial applicability; see Chapter 7 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficient disclosure / enablement (scope of substantive examination item 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must provide sufficient details to enable a PSIA to practise the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enablement requirements are detailed in Chapter 8.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty (scope of substantive examination item 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The claimed invention must be new — not in public use or known by others prior to the effective filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty considerations are detailed in Chapter 10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventive step / non-obviousness (scope of substantive examination item 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention must involve an inventive step — not obvious to a PSIA in view of the prior art on the effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventive step analysis is detailed in Chapter 11.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability (scope of substantive examination item 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The invention must be capable of industrial application — able to be made or used in some industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further guidance is in Chapter 12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options for expediting substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanisms exist to accelerate substantive examination including bilateral PPH, regional PPH (ASPEC programmes), and national fast-track programmes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PPH allows an applicant to request accelerated examination at an office of later examination when claims are found patentable by an office of first filing/examination. ASEAN regional programmes include ASPEC Prosecution Highway, PCT-ASPEC programme, and ASPEC for Industry 4.0. National fast-track schemes exist in Malaysia, Thailand (pilot), and Singapore (with caps and conditions such as applicant residency, limits per entity, requirement to indicate reasons). Specific caps, fees and expected grant timelines vary by program and country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment timing of patentable subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of patentable subject-matter is typically conducted during substantive examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because assessment is complex it is recommended to be done by examiners versed in patentability conditions. Exception: Viet Nam assesses subject-matter in both formalities and substantive examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability of substantive examination reports to third parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive examination reports should be made available to third parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They should be accessible at the latest after the granting date of a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal and response to substantive examination reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may respond to objections with explanations, data or evidence; if rejection is maintained the applicant may appeal to an upper administrative body or court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admissibility of responses depends on the case. Appeal procedures (administrative and judicial) are available and follow national rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds and procedure for appeal of substantive examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Following receipt of the substantive examination report, an applicant may file an appeal against a decision rejecting a patent based on unresolved objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals can proceed through administrative and judicial procedures in accordance with national law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and minimum content of substantive examination report
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantive examination reports should contain minimum specified information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum information includes: assessment of patentability of the invention; search report (if applicable); list and details of cited prior art (patent and non-patent literature); grounds for rejecting the application and explanation; and the deadline to respond to an objection.
